column1: # claim_check retro-scan, 2026-09-25: MAIN's tools/claim_check.py (7e2edc08e, standalone <!--derived--> runs to the next '## ' heading)
# Run inside the round-4 worktree, so both checkers resolve the SAME artifacts (research/findings/raw files that are
# untracked in the primary checkout are absent here for BOTH; a 'missing artifact' reason is shared, not new).
# Populations: (a) research/findings/*.md ADDED on main since 2026-09-01 (git log --since=2026-09-01 --diff-filter=A):
# 353 paths, 351 on disk; (b) the whole corpus, research/findings/*.md: 2970 docs.
#     of which round 4 flags MORE numbers         6                   21   (docs where round 4 flags FEWER: 0)
# main-pass/new-fail reasons (a): {'unsupported number': 33, 'unsupported number + low coverage': 1}
# main-pass/new-fail reasons (b): {'unsupported number': 152, 'unsupported number + low coverage': 1, 'low coverage': 15}
# WHY each flagged line moved (column scope_change; flagged LINES, whole corpus): the marker's scope used to run to the
# next '## ' heading and now covers only its next paragraph/list/table, so a number in a LATER block of the same
# section is checked ('later block in the same section'); a marker directly before a heading, a fence or a non-comment
# html block now covers nothing; a lazy continuation line after a list item is checked; a marker inside a fence is text.
# Classification is descriptive (scratch script, same parser), not part of the checker.
# A FLAG IS NOT PROOF OF AN ERROR. 'unsupported number' means the number does not appear in any cited artifact within
# tolerance and is no longer inside a derived scope. Many flagged numbers are legitimate re-quotes, rounded means or
# differences whose author relied on the old section-wide scope and would now mark them inline or with a range; some
# may be genuine errors. This scan did not read them. The board (GAP_CLOSURE_MISSION.md, 02:55 claim-check entry)
# records audit branches research/claimcheck-audit-1..4 with 8 corrections from a manual pass over ROUND 2's flags;
# those edits are not merged and not reflected here. 'low coverage' = >= 40 numeric claims with < 5% checked.
# claim_check runs only on newly ADDED findings at commit, so none of these legacy docs blocks anything.
# Columns: doc | population | direction | new_reasons | main_reasons | new_unsupported_n | new_unsupported (line=value,
# first 6) | new_checked/total | new_suppressed_by_mechanism | scope_change (flagged lines by cause)
